question: What defines a portal circulatory system?

options.A: A vein connecting two capillary beds
options.C: A direct shunt from vein to artery
options.D: An artery feeding directly into an organ

explanation: A portal system uniquely links one capillary network to another via a connecting vessel before returning to the heart. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h1)

question: Why is portal circulation different from normal systemic blood flow?

options.A: It bypasses the heart completely to save energy
options.B: It operates entirely without capillary exchange
options.C: It delivers blood between two capillary networks directly
options.D: It carries only oxygenated blood to abdominal organs

explanation: Unlike standard circulation which goes capillary-vein-heart, portal systems route blood from one capillary bed to a second one before cardiac return. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h1)

question: Which two major vessels join to form the hepatic portal vein?

options.B: Inferior vena cava and abdominal aorta
options.C: Gastric vein and inferior mesenteric vein
options.D: Superior mesenteric vein and splenic vein

explanation: The confluence of the superior mesenteric vein and the splenic vein creates the main hepatic portal vein trunk. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h2)

question: What type of blood does the hepatic portal vein primarily carry to the liver?

options.A: Fatty acids absorbed directly into lymph
options.B: Lymph fluid filtered from the kidneys
options.C: Purely oxygenated blood from the lungs

explanation: Blood entering the liver via the portal vein has already passed through GI capillaries, meaning it is low in oxygen but high in absorbed nutrients. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h2)

question: What is the primary effect of first-pass metabolism on oral medications?

options.C: Complete conversion into red blood cells

explanation: Liver enzymes break down a portion of ingested drugs before they reach the rest of the body, lowering their systemic availability. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h3)

question: A patient with severe liver disease is prescribed an oral drug with high first-pass clearance. What is the main clinical concern?

options.A: Immediate allergic reaction in the GI tract
options.B: Risk of drug toxicity due to reduced metabolism
options.C: Complete failure of the drug to dissolve in water
options.D: Rapid elimination of the drug through the skin

explanation: When liver function is compromised, first-pass breakdown drops, leading to higher-than-expected drug levels in the blood and potential toxicity. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h3)

question: Which two structures are connected by the hypophysial portal system?
explanation: The hypophysial portal vessels link the base of the brain to the anterior pituitary to deliver releasing hormones. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h4)

question: Why does the body use a portal system for hypothalamic-pituitary communication?

options.A: To deliver releasing hormones directly in high concentrations
options.B: To cool down the brain during high metabolic activity
options.C: To filter out large blood proteins before hormone release
options.D: To mix endocrine secretions directly with digestive enzymes

explanation: Direct vascular linkage prevents hormones from being diluted throughout the entire systemic circulation before reaching the pituitary. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h4)

question: What is the most common underlying cause of portal hypertension?
explanation: Scarring and structural changes in cirrhotic livers obstruct blood flow, raising pressure within the portal vein. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h5)

question: Why do esophageal varices develop in patients with portal hypertension?

options.A: Excess dietary protein creates venous blockages
options.B: Stomach acid erodes the lower esophageal sphincter
options.C: High systemic blood pressure bursts heart valves
options.D: Blood bypasses the blocked liver through collateral vessels

explanation: Elevated portal pressure forces blood into smaller, fragile collateral veins connecting the portal system to the systemic circulation, such as those in the esophagus. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h5)

question: Which symptom is a major indicator of hepatic encephalopathy in liver failure patients?

options.A: Severe pain in the right lower quadrant
options.B: Inability to move the lower extremities

explanation: The buildup of neurotoxins like ammonia in the blood due to poor liver filtering leads to confusion and cognitive changes. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h6)

question: A patient with portal hypertension and ascites is admitted to the ward. Which nursing action is most appropriate?

options.A: Measure daily abdominal girth and track strict fluid balance
options.B: Provide vigorous abdominal massage to relieve fluid pressure
options.C: Encourage a high-protein diet to rebuild liver tissue quickly
options.D: Administer intramuscular injections for pain relief regularly

explanation: Tracking weight and abdominal girth helps monitor fluid retention and the effectiveness of diuretic therapy in ascites. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T11#GNS111_U2_T11_h6)
